citation: Guil JL, Rodríguez-García I, Torija E. Plant Foods Hum Nutr. 1997;51(2):99-107.
scope: 16 wild edible plant species, human-food composition
finding: Oxalic acid and nitrate varied widely among species; Plantago major had low erucic acid reported (3.45%).
limitation: Not a tortoise toxicity study; does not establish a safe tortoise dose.

finding: Leafy plant foods are important dietary oxalate sources and measured values vary by food and processing.
limitation: Human-food review; use for chemistry context, not tortoise clinical thresholds.

citation: Food oxalate: factors affecting measurement, biological variation, and bioavailability.
finding: Oxalate values can vary with analytical method, cultivar, harvest time and growing conditions.
limitation: Does not provide a universal plant safety cutoff.

citation: Am J Clin Nutr. 2025. Nitrate and nitrite food composition database update.
finding: Nitrate/nitrite values show seasonal, geographic and cooking-related variation.
limitation: Human food database; not a Testudo toxicity threshold.

citation: Plantago major in Traditional Persian Medicine and modern phytotherapy: a narrative review.
finding: Reviews botanical characterization, phytochemistry, pharmacology and toxicity literature for P. major.
limitation: Not tortoise-specific and not equivalent to a feeding recommendation.

citation: Systematic review of Taraxacum chemodiversity, pharmacology and toxicology.
finding: Documents substantial species-level chemodiversity and differences across Taraxacum.
limitation: Supports identity caution; does not prove all Taraxacum taxa interchangeable for tortoise feeding.

citation: Adom MB et al. Biomed Pharmacother. 2017;96:348-360. DOI 10.1016/j.biopha.2017.09.152
finding: Reviews chemical constituents including flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, phenolic acid derivatives and iridoid glycosides.
limitation: Not tortoise-specific; constituent presence is not a tortoise toxicity threshold.

citation: Evaluation of Major Minerals and Trace Elements in Wild and Domesticated Edible Herbs Traditionally Used in the Mediterranean Area. DOI 10.1007/s12011-020-02467-3
scope: Cichorium intybus, Plantago coronopus and two other edible herbs
finding: Measured major/trace minerals and evaluated nitrate and oxalate under wild and domesticated growing conditions.
limitation: Human-food composition study; C. intybus/Plantago coronopus cannot be automatically mapped to every Korean retail chicory/plantain.
